# Spec: 005-gamificacao
<!-- Generated by /speckit.specify -->
<!-- Date: 2026-09-12 -->

## Overview

The XP ledger and everything that reads it: skills and levels, the per-organization skill
catalogue an admin can change without moving anyone's progress, missions validated by the lab
team, the makers' ranking and the collective Nível do Lab.

This is the feature `packages/game` was created empty for in 000, and the feature constitution
Principle 3 is written about. Its economy was closed by the PO on 2026-08-23/24 —
`docs/product/gamification.md` records all eight of its own open questions as **decided** — so
this spec records decisions rather than discovering them.

## What already exists, and what this feature adds

Verified on disk at `dev` 62cb076, not taken from the features' specs.

| Already shipped | By | What 005 does with it |
|---|---|---|
| `skill` — scoped, `nome`/`slug`/`ativa` | 004 | adds the admin flow and the deactivation/reactivation **semantics**; the storage exists |
| `perfilMaker.skills[] = { skill, nivel, xp }` | 004 | fills it. Assigned at signup at level 0 for every active skill |
| `progressoAula` — `{ aula, usuario, percentualAssistido, posicaoReproducao, concluidaEm }` | 002 | `concluidaEm` is the artifact that credits a watched class |
| `aprovacaoRegistrada` + `aprovadoEm` on `projeto`, `artigo`, `aula`, `modelo3d`, `evento` | 002 | 002's CLR-001 kept the *record* there and gave 005 **the ledger**. That pair is what credits a publication |
| `lib/content/counters.ts` — recompute-from-source inside the writing transaction | 002 | the discipline every XP projection follows |
| `lib/tenancy/seed-on-create.ts` | 000 | seeds `regrasXp` when an organization is created |
| `packages/game` — empty, with a Payload/Next import fence | 000 | receives the rules |

**`perfilMaker` carries no overall XP total and no overall level.** Every public page prints
level 1 today as a documented stand-in and says so in its source. Giving a maker an overall
level is this feature's.

**`projeto` carries no `autor` at all.** `Projeto.ts` defers it to 005 **by name**, and four
page files credit "Fab Lab" as a placeholder each saying *"Delete this the moment `autor`
exists"*. It lands here — see CLR-002.

## User Scenarios

### US1: Publishing earns XP, once [P1]

- **Given** a maker of this lab whose article is in the review queue
- **When** the team approves it and the publication is stamped
- **Then** one ledger entry is written **inside the same transaction**, the maker's XP and the
  skill's XP each rise by 1, and the entry records who, what action, and which content
- **Edge**: the team un-publishes and re-approves the same article — the ledger already holds
  an entry for that content, so **nothing is credited a second time** and no error is shown
- **Error**: the ledger write fails — the approval fails with it and the article stays
  unpublished, because a publication that credited nothing is a silent debt

### US2: Watching a class to the end earns XP [P1]

- **Given** a signed-in maker with a `progressoAula` row for a class
- **When** the row reaches 100% and `concluidaEm` is stamped
- **Then** one XP is credited to the maker and to the class's skill, keyed on that class
- **Edge**: they watch the same class again — `concluidaEm` is already set, the ledger already
  holds the entry, and **no second XP is credited however many times it is rewatched**
- **Error**: a request claims completion for a class that has no progress row for this maker —
  it is refused, and no ledger entry is written

### US3: A mission is completed and the team validates it [P1]

- **Given** a mission published by the team, and a maker who submits their proof
- **When** a member of the team approves the submission
- **Then** one XP is credited, to the maker and to **the skill the mission names**, and the
  maker's submission moves to an approved state
- **Edge**: two team members approve the same submission — the second approval credits nothing
- **Error**: the maker submits twice for the same mission — the second submission is refused,
  because a mission is completed once

### US4: An admin changes the skill catalogue without moving anyone's XP [P1]

- **Given** a lab whose makers hold levels in `Corte a Laser`
- **When** the organization's admin **removes** that skill
- **Then** it is **deactivated** (`ativa: false`), every ledger entry stays, every maker's XP
  total is unchanged, and the skill stops being offered for new work
- **Edge**: the admin **reactivates** it — every maker's level in it **reappears** at exactly
  the value it had, because the projection is recomputed from an untouched ledger
- **Error**: the admin tries to hard-delete a skill that has ledger entries — it is refused
  with a message naming the count, because deleting it would make history unreadable

### US5: A new skill starts everyone at level 0 [P2]

- **Given** a lab whose makers signed up before `Serigrafia` existed
- **When** the admin adds it
- **Then** **every** maker of that lab carries it at level 0 — the assignment is not only a
  signup-time act
- **Edge**: a maker signs up afterwards — they get the same catalogue, at level 0
- **Error**: adding a skill whose `slug` already exists in this lab is refused

### US6: The ranking shows this lab's makers, by XP [P2]

- **Given** several makers of this lab with different totals
- **When** the ranking is read
- **Then** it lists them highest first, with each maker's avatar, `@handle` and XP total
- **Edge**: two makers are tied — the order is **stable and declared**, never arbitrary
- **Error**: a maker of another lab never appears, whatever their total

### US7: XP does not sum between labs [P1]

- **Given** one login with a profile at lab A and a profile at lab B
- **When** they earn XP at A
- **Then** the profile at B is unchanged — a different total, a different level, a different
  place in a different ranking
- **Edge**: a skill with the same `slug` exists at both labs — they are two rows and two
  progressions
- **Error**: no read of A's ledger, ranking or lab level ever returns a row of B's

### US8: The Nível do Lab aggregates the community [P2]

- **Given** the ledger of one organization
- **When** the lab's level is read
- **Then** it is the same curve every other level uses — 5 XP per level, capped at 10 — over
  the organization's total
- **Edge**: a lab with no XP at all reads level 0 with an empty bar, never a blank card
- **Error**: it never counts XP from another organization

### US9: A maker sees their real skills on Minha Conta [P2]

- **Given** a maker with progress in three skills
- **When** they open Minha Conta
- **Then** the SUAS SKILLS panel shows each **active** skill with its real level, as a
  ten-segment pip bar, starting empty at level 0
- **Edge**: a skill they hold progress in was deactivated — it is **not** shown, and their XP
  total does not change
- **Error**: nothing on the screen awards XP; it is a read

### US10: A project credits its author [P2]

- **Given** a project published by a maker
- **When** the card and the project page render
- **Then** they credit that maker — name, `@handle` and their real level — instead of the
  "Fab Lab" placeholder four pages carry today
- **Edge**: the author's account was erased — 004's tombstone renders, and the project keeps
  its place
- **Error**: a project with no author is never rendered with a fabricated one

## Functional Requirements

### The ledger and the rules

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Scenario |
|----|-------------|----------|----------|
| FR-001 | An XP ledger collection, **scoped** and **append-only**: no update, no delete, by access control | P1 | US1 |
| FR-002 | Every entry records the organization, the maker's profile, the action, the content it refers to, the skill credited, the amount, and when | P1 | US1 |
| FR-003 | `idempotencyKey = (tenant, user, action, ref)` enforced by a **unique index** — constitution Principle 3, verbatim | P1 | US1 |
| FR-004 | XP is granted **inside the same transaction as the action that caused it**, never by a later job | P1 | US1 |
| FR-005 | The economy lives in `packages/game` as pure functions — no Payload import, no IO, `tenantId` an explicit argument | P1 | US1 |
| FR-006 | 1 XP per action; the actions are exactly: watch a class to 100%, publish a project, publish a 3D model, publish an article, complete a mission | P1 | US1 |
| FR-007 | `nivel = min(rules.nivelMaximo, floor(xp / rules.xpPorNivel))` — one rule for the maker, each skill and the lab. The CITe seed is 5 XP per level, cap 10; the **rule** is the requirement and the **numbers are data** (CLR-010) | P1 | US1 |
| FR-008 | Likes award no XP, and calendar attendance awards none in v1 | P1 | US1 |
| FR-009 | `regrasXp` is **per-organization data**, seeded on organization creation from the CITe default — retuning the economy is an edit, not a deploy | P1 | US7 |

### The projections

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Scenario |
|----|-------------|----------|----------|
| FR-010 | A maker's XP total and level, and each skill's XP and level, are **projections of the ledger**, maintained the way `counters.ts` maintains counters: recomputed from source rows inside the writing transaction | P1 | US1 |
| FR-011 | A reconciliation gate recomputes every projection from the ledger and **fails CI** on any disagreement, as `counters.ts` already does for counters. Nothing repairs at runtime (CLR-014) | P1 | US1 |
| FR-012 | The Nível do Lab is a projection of the organization's whole ledger, on the same curve | P2 | US8 |
| FR-013 | The ranking orders this organization's makers by XP total, highest first, with a **declared tie-break** | P2 | US6 |

### The skill catalogue

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Scenario |
|----|-------------|----------|----------|
| FR-014 | The organization's admin can add and deactivate skills; the five CITe skills are the seed | P1 | US4 |
| FR-015 | Removal is **deactivation** (`ativa: false`). The ledger is untouched and no maker's total changes | P1 | US4 |
| FR-016 | Reactivating a skill makes every maker's level in it reappear at its previous value | P1 | US4 |
| FR-017 | Adding a skill assigns it at level 0 to **every** maker of that organization, not only to new ones | P2 | US5 |
| FR-018 | A skill with ledger entries cannot be hard-deleted; the refusal names how many entries exist | P2 | US4 |
| FR-019 | A deactivated skill is hidden from the maker's panel and from new mission and content assignment, without changing stored progress | P2 | US9 |

### Missions

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Scenario |
|----|-------------|----------|----------|
| FR-020 | A `missao` collection, **scoped**, carrying a title, a description, an icon, the skill it credits, and a published state | P1 | US3 |
| FR-021 | A maker submits a completion for a mission; the team approves or rejects it in the review queue 002 built | P1 | US3 |
| FR-022 | The XP credits **on approval**, once, through the same idempotency key as every other action | P1 | US3 |
| FR-023 | **One submission row per mission per maker, forever**, enforced by a unique index. A rejection does not bar the maker: the row is **reopened** (CLR-015) | P2 | US3 |
| FR-024 | A mission's progress shown to a maker is **their own**; a signed-out visitor sees the mission with no personal percentage and an invitation to sign in | P2 | US3 |
| FR-036 | A submission carries **one photo**, as a `midiaImagem` relationship — never a text key, never a second upload route (CLR-006). Missions therefore sit on the upload trust boundary, and constitution Principle 5's security review applies to them | P1 | US3 |

### Anti-farm and trust

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Scenario |
|----|-------------|----------|----------|
| FR-025 | Idempotency is per content: a class credits once **ever**, however many times it is rewatched; a publication credits once per content, across unpublish/republish cycles | P1 | US2 |
| FR-026 | There is no daily cap in v1 — the decision of 2026-08-24, recorded so its absence is deliberate | P2 | US2 |
| FR-027 | A completion claim for a class with no progress row belonging to the requesting maker is refused | P1 | US2 |
| FR-039 | `projeto`, `artigo`, `aula` and `modelo3d` each carry a **`skill`** relationship, nullable, naming the skill a publication credits (CLR-009). A publication with none credits the maker's total and no skill | P1 | US1 |
| FR-040 | Deleting a profile **nulls** `xpLedger.perfil` on its entries and changes nothing else; every reader tolerates an entry with no profile (CLR-011) | P1 | US7 |
| FR-041 | A rejected submission returns to `enviada` when the maker edits it — one row, reopened (CLR-015) | P2 | US3 |
| FR-042 | The credit hook is registered on **four** collections, never on `evento` (CLR-012) | P1 | US1 |
| FR-043 | `xpTotal` is uncapped; only `nivel` stops at the cap, and the pip bar stays full there (CLR-013) | P1 | US6 |
| FR-038 | Beyond FR-027, a class completion is **trusted** in v1 — no elapsed-time floor, no checkpoints (CLR-008). The ledger is the audit trail: every credit carries who, what and when, and is append-only, so farming is bounded and visible rather than prevented | P2 | US2 |

### Multi-tenancy

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Scenario |
|----|-------------|----------|----------|
| FR-028 | The ledger, `regrasXp`, `missao` and every mission submission are **scoped**, declared in `scope-registry.ts` with their reason and in an order `resetWorld` can walk backwards | P1 | US7 |
| FR-029 | XP never sums between organizations; every projection, ranking and lab level is confined to one | P1 | US7 |
| FR-030 | Every scoped→scoped relationship this feature adds carries the shared `sameTenant` validator | P1 | US7 |
| FR-031 | This feature adds **no fourth door** to `lib/tenancy`. Every read and write here belongs to a signed-in maker or the team, so `getTenantScopedPayload(req)` serves it — and if that turns out to be false, it is a finding to report with the measurement, not a door to open quietly | P1 | US7 |

### The surfaces this feature owns

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Scenario |
|----|-------------|----------|----------|
| FR-032 | Minha Conta's SUAS SKILLS panel shows real levels — ten pips, empty at level 0 | P2 | US9 |
| FR-033 | The author strip on cards and detail pages shows the maker's **real** level, replacing the level-1 stand-in four pages document | P2 | US10 |
| FR-034 | `projeto` gains its `autor` relationship, nullable from the start so it never needs 004's tombstone migration (CLR-002) | P2 | US10 |
| FR-037 | A `/ranking` page ships **here**, showing this organization's makers by XP with the declared tie-break — the destination of the `VER RANKING COMPLETO` link 006's Home card will carry (CLR-007) | P2 | US6 |
| FR-035 | The isolation harness gains a vantage point for the ledger: a maker of A gets zero rows on every XP surface of B, demonstrated failing before passing | P1 | US7 |

## Success Criteria

| ID | Criterion | Validation Method |
|----|-----------|-------------------|
| SC-001 | Approving the same publication twice writes exactly one ledger entry | integration test driving a real approve → unpublish → approve cycle |
| SC-002 | The unique index refuses a duplicate `(tenant, user, action, ref)` at the database, not only in application code | a test that inserts the duplicate directly and asserts `23505` |
| SC-003 | A failed ledger write rolls the approval back — no published content without its entry | a test with a rejecting ledger, asserting the content is still unpublished |
| SC-004 | Every projection equals a recount of the ledger, across the whole database | a reconciliation gate, in the shape `counters.test.ts` already uses |
| SC-005 | `packages/game` imports nothing from Payload or Next | the existing import fence, extended to the new modules |
| SC-006 | Level arithmetic matches the rule against **injected** rules, and the CITe seed's table (0→0, 5→1, 49→9, 50→10, 999→10) is one case of it — never the definition (CLR-010) | a table test over the pure function, plus one with a different cap |
| SC-007 | Deactivating a skill changes no `xp` value anywhere | a test that records every total, deactivates, and re-reads |
| SC-008 | Reactivating restores every level to its previous value | the same test, continued |
| SC-009 | Adding a skill gives it at level 0 to a maker who signed up before it existed | an integration test |
| SC-010 | A maker of organization A reads zero rows on every XP surface of B | `scripts/isolation-mutation.sh` gains a layer, watched red with a planted violation |
| SC-011 | Rewatching a class credits nothing the second time | an integration test driving two completions |
| SC-012 | A mission approved by two people credits once | an integration test |
| SC-013 | The ranking's tie-break is deterministic across runs | a test with two makers at equal XP, asserting a stable order |
| SC-014 | The lab level of an empty lab reads 0, not blank or `NaN` | a test on a lab with no ledger entries |
| SC-015 | No public page gains a client boundary — the island count is unchanged | `islands.test.ts` |
| SC-016 | The six public pages stay inside the LCP budget | `scripts/lcp-budget.sh` |
| SC-017 | A mission submission stores a `midiaImagem` id, never a key, a URL or a filename | a test feeding each of those four shapes and asserting the write is refused |
| SC-018 | `/ranking` answers for a signed-in maker and never lists another organization's makers | an integration test, plus the isolation layer of SC-010 |
| SC-019 | Every XP credit is reconstructible from the ledger alone — who, what, when | a test that rebuilds one maker's history from entries only |
| SC-020 | Publishing an `evento` credits nothing | an integration test approving an event and asserting zero entries |
| SC-021 | Erasing a profile leaves its entries with `perfil` null, and the lab level is unchanged | an integration test around 004's `deleteAccount` |
| SC-022 | A rejected submission can be reopened and approved, crediting once | an integration test driving reject → edit → approve |

## Clarifications

Every question this spec opened is now decided. Three were put to the PO on 2026-09-12 and are
recorded as CLR-006, CLR-007 and CLR-008; the other five were decided while writing it.

### CLR-001: The ledger is the source of truth and every aggregate is a projection [architecture] — decided 2026-09-12

**Decision**: `perfilMaker.xp`, each skill's `nivel`/`xp`, the lab level and the ranking are all
**derived**. They are stored for reading, maintained inside the writing transaction, and
reconcilable against the ledger at any time. When a projection and the ledger disagree, the
ledger is right and the projection is repaired **by re-running the maintenance — which CI
requires before merge (CLR-014 narrows this: there is no runtime repair)**.

**Rationale**: constitution Principle 3 makes the ledger append-only and idempotent; that only
buys something if nothing else is authoritative. `counters.ts` already established this exact
discipline for the like and download counters — recompute from source rows inside the writing
transaction, plus a reconciliation gate that fails on drift — and a second mechanism for the
same guarantee would be a second thing to get wrong.

**Impact**: FR-010, FR-011, FR-012, FR-013, SC-004.

### CLR-002: `projeto.autor` lands in 005, nullable from the start [scope] — decided 2026-09-12

**Decision**: this feature adds `autor` to `projeto` as a **nullable** relationship to
`perfilMaker`, and deletes the `AUTORIA_PENDENTE` placeholder from the four page files that
carry it.

**Rationale**: `Projeto.ts` defers it to 005 by name, and `page.tsx`, `projetos/page.tsx` and
two others each carry the same constant with the same instruction — *"Delete this the moment
`autor` exists, here and there, in one change."* FR-033 needs a real author to read a real
level from, so the two arrive together or neither does.

Nullable from the start is 004's lesson paid forward: making `autor` nullable on the other three
collections needed a migration **and** the removal of `required: true`, because `push` rebuilds
every non-production schema from the field config and `sameTenant` re-implements the `required`
floor. A column that is nullable on the day it is created needs none of that.

**Impact**: FR-034, FR-033, US10.

### CLR-003: No fourth tenancy door [architecture] — decided 2026-09-12

**Decision**: this feature adds nothing to `PUBLIC_GLOBAL_CATALOGUE`, `getSignupScopedPayload`
or `getErasureScopedPayload`, and creates no new one.

**Rationale**: every operation here belongs to somebody who is signed in — a maker earning,
a maker reading their own panel, the team approving — and `getTenantScopedPayload(req)` is
built for exactly that. 004 opened three doors because three operations genuinely had no path;
each cost an argument and a gate. If an operation here turns out to be refused, **that is a
finding to report with the measurement**, not a reason to widen a door.

The one to watch is the ranking read on the logged-in Home: it crosses profiles within one
organization, which is ordinary scoped reading, not a bypass.

**Impact**: FR-031.

### CLR-004: 006 keeps the Home; 005 ships no gamified panel [scope] — decided 2026-09-12

**Decision**: 005 ships the mechanics, the data and Minha Conta's skills panel. The
`MISSÕES EM DESTAQUE`, `NÍVEL DO LAB` and `RANKING MAKERS` cards on the logged-in Home are
feature 006's, and 003's public Home continues to ship none of them.

**Rationale**: `sdd-strategy.md` splits them that way, and 003's CLR-004 already refused to
render those panels against tables that did not exist — *"the page would not fail loudly, it
would render zeroes … which is worse than not shipping them, because it looks like the product
working"*. With the tables existing, the panels become buildable; that does not make them this
feature's.

**Impact**: FR-032, SC-015, and the boundary 006 inherits.

### CLR-005: Level 0 is a real level [design] — decided 2026-09-12

**Decision**: the scale runs 0–10. A maker and a skill both start at **0** with an empty pip
bar, and `minha-conta.md` round 4 says so explicitly.

**Rationale**: it is already shipped — `perfilMaker.skills[].nivel` has `defaultValue: 0` and
its admin description cites the decision. The mockups' `NÍVEL 1 com 1 pip` is struck through in
the source. This is recorded because *"5 XP per level"* with a cap of 10 invites an off-by-one:
50 XP is level 10, and 0 XP is not level 1.

**Impact**: FR-007, SC-006, SC-014.

### CLR-006: A mission's proof is a photo, through `midiaImagem` [design] — decided 2026-09-12

**Decision**: a maker completing a mission attaches **one photo**, stored as a `midiaImagem`
relationship like every other image in the product. Not a free-text note, and not nothing.

**Rationale**: `gamification.md` § Missões names *"o anexo de comprovação (foto/arquivo)"* and
leaves only the format open, so a photo is the reading closest to the source. It also reuses a
path that already exists and is already tested: 002's presigned PUT, its post-upload
verification and its size limits, and decision D3's rule that **media is a relationship, never a
text key**. A second upload route for one collection would be the thing that route exists to
prevent.

**What it costs, stated rather than discovered**: missions now touch the **upload trust
boundary**, so constitution Principle 5's mandatory security review applies to them. A mission
submission carries user-controlled content, and the reviewer opening the queue is looking at a
file a stranger uploaded.

**Impact**: FR-020, FR-021, FR-036, US3.

### CLR-007: `/ranking` ships here, with the mechanics [scope] — decided 2026-09-12

**Decision**: the full ranking page is **005's**. Feature 006's Home card shows the top five and
links to it.

**Rationale**: 005 computes the ranking, so the page reads data that exists the moment it does —
and the alternative is a footer link to a 404 for however long 006 takes. That is precisely the
half-shipped state 003's CLR-010 cost a whole feature to close: a control that renders and
answers with nothing. Shipping the destination with the computation makes 006's card a link to
something that works.

**Impact**: FR-037, FR-013, US6, and the boundary CLR-004 draws with 006.

### CLR-008: A class completion is trusted in v1, and the ledger is the audit trail [security] — decided 2026-09-12

**Decision**: v1 accepts the client's claim that a class was watched to the end. No elapsed-time
floor, no server-side checkpoints. FR-027's rule stands — a claim needs a progress row belonging
to the requesting maker — and idempotency caps the gain at 1 XP per class, forever.

**Rationale**: the honest-community assumption, consistent with the posture already decided on
2026-08-24 (*"sem limite diário no v1"*). The gain is bounded by the catalogue, every credit is
a ledger row carrying who, what and when, and the ledger is append-only — so a maker who claimed
forty classes in four minutes is **visible after the fact**, by inspection, without any
instrumentation being built first.

**What this deliberately does not claim**: that farming is prevented. It is not. It is bounded
and auditable, which is a different and weaker property, and the decision is revisitable once
the game is running — the two options costed were an elapsed-time floor against `duracaoMin`
(cheap, beatable by waiting) and real progress checkpoints (strong, needs player integration and
changes `progressoAula`'s write path).

**Impact**: FR-026, FR-027, FR-038.

### CLR-009: A publication credits the skill its content names [design] — decided 2026-09-13

**Decision**: `projeto`, `artigo`, `aula` and `modelo3d` each gain a **`skill` relationship**,
chosen by the author and visible to the team at approval. That is the skill the ledger entry
credits.

**Rationale**: found by CHK010/011 — FR-002 requires the entry to record a skill and **nothing
mapped a publication to one**. A project has a `categoria`; an article and a model have neither,
and the three category vocabularies are independent of each other, so a category→skill mapping
would have been a fourth vocabulary to seed and keep in step.

Naming the skill on the content is the honest shape: a laser-cut piece credits *Corte a Laser*
because its author said so, and the team confirms it in the same review that publishes it.
`gamification.md` assumes exactly this when it says makers evolve skills *"pelo jogo — publicar
modelos 3D, assistir aulas, publicar projetos"*.

**Impact**: FR-039 (new), FR-002, FR-006. Four shipped collections gain a field and a migration.
**Nullable**, for the reason CLR-002 already gives: a column created nullable never needs 004's
two-layer `required: true` repair, and the content published before this feature has no skill to
name. A publication with no skill credits the maker's total and no skill — which is also what
the review queue is for.

### CLR-010: `regrasXp` is the authority; 10 is the seed [architecture] — decided 2026-09-13

**Decision**: the level cap, the XP per action and the XP per level are **whatever
`regrasXp` says** for that organization. The numbers in `gamification.md` and in this spec are
the **CITe defaults**, seeded on organization creation.

**Rationale**: found by CHK001 — FR-007 stated the cap as a requirement while FR-009 made it
editable data, and the two cannot both be true. Constitution Principle 3 breaks the tie in one
sentence: *"retuning XP is an edit, not a deploy."*

**What this changes about testing, which is the part that matters**: a test asserting *"the cap
is 10"* is asserting a **seed value**, and it fails on a lab that retuned legitimately. Tests
assert the **rule** — `levelFor(xp, rules) === min(rules.nivelMaximo, floor(xp / rules.xpPorNivel))`
— against **injected** rules. SC-006's table becomes a table over the CITe defaults, named as
such.

**Impact**: FR-007, FR-009, SC-006, and every task that would otherwise have hard-coded a 10.

### CLR-011: An erased maker's entries survive, anonymised [data-lifecycle] — decided 2026-09-13

**Decision**: deleting a profile (004's FR-031) **nulls** `xpLedger.perfil` on that maker's
entries and leaves everything else — skill, action, ref, amount, timestamp — untouched.

**Rationale**: found by CHK013. It is 004's tombstone applied to the ledger, and for the same
reason: *the work stays, the name goes*. The lab's collective level (FR-012) stays honest,
because the XP was really earned; the ranking simply loses a row; and FR-001's append-only
survives, because nulling one column is not rewriting history — the deletion itself is the
historical event.

The two rejected alternatives each broke something: deleting the entries would rewrite history
*and* silently drop the lab's level when somebody leaves; leaving a dangling reference is the
exact shape 004's phase 6 spent a round repairing.

**Impact**: FR-040 (new), FR-001, FR-012, FR-013. `xpLedger.perfil` is **nullable**, and every
reader — ranking, reconciliation, lab level — is written knowing an entry may have no profile.
`docs/lgpd.md` gains a row saying what deletion does to XP.

### CLR-012: Publishing an EVENT scores nothing [scope] — decided 2026-09-13

**Decision**: the credit hook is registered on **four** collections — `projeto`, `artigo`,
`aula`, `modelo3d` — and **not** on `evento`.

**Rationale**: found by CHK002, and it is the cheapest bug this checklist prevented. `evento`
carries `aprovacaoRegistrada` exactly like the other four, so *"register the hook on the
reviewable collections"* would have credited event publication — which FR-008 forbids in one
line, and which question 4 of `gamification.md` decided on 2026-08-24: *"o calendário não
concede XP por enquanto"*.

**Impact**: FR-006, FR-008, and T017's wording.

### CLR-013: `xpTotal` is uncapped; only `nivel` stops at the cap [design] — decided 2026-09-13

**Decision**: a maker's `xpTotal` keeps rising forever. `nivel` is
`min(cap, floor(xpTotal / perLevel))`, and the pip bar stays **full** at the cap rather than
resetting.

**Rationale**: found by CHK003/CHK004. FR-013 sorts the ranking by XP total — if the total
capped with the level, every maker at the cap would tie permanently and the ranking would stop
being one. A bar that reset to empty at the top would read as a demotion.

**Impact**: FR-007, FR-013, FR-032, SC-006.

### CLR-014: The reconciliation is a CI gate, not a runtime repair [architecture] — decided 2026-09-13

**Decision**: FR-011's reconciliation runs in CI and **fails the build** on drift. Nothing
repairs a projection at runtime.

**Rationale**: found by CHK006, which noticed FR-011 describes a *test* while CLR-001 says a
disagreeing projection *"is repaired"*. The same question was answered for the like and download
counters in 002, and this feature should not answer it differently: `counters.ts` says in its own
docstring that a stored value goes stale through a path the hook never sees — an admin bulk
delete, a migration, a manual SQL fix — and that *"nothing fails when that happens"* until the
gate runs.

Consistency is the argument. A runtime repair here and none there would mean two disciplines for
one guarantee, which is what CLR-001 exists to prevent.

**Impact**: FR-011 is reworded from "reports any disagreement" to "fails CI on any
disagreement". CLR-001's *"is repaired"* becomes *"is repaired by re-running the maintenance,
which CI requires before merge"*.

### CLR-015: A rejected submission is reopened, never replaced [design] — decided 2026-09-13

**Decision**: there is **one `missaoSubmissao` row per (mission, maker), forever**. A rejection
sets its status to `recusada`; the maker edits it — a new photo, a new note — and it returns to
`enviada`.

**Rationale**: found by CHK017. The unique index FR-023 asks for would otherwise bar a maker
permanently after one rejection, which is punitive and certainly not intended: a rejection means
*"not yet"*, and a review queue whose only outcome is exile is not a review queue.

Reopening keeps the constraint as a **database guarantee** rather than a partial index or an
application check, and it keeps the review history in one row where a team member can see that
this is the second attempt.

**Impact**: FR-023 is reworded — one submission per mission per maker, reopenable — and FR-041
(new) carries the reopen transition.
